title: Solving sin^2(theta) = cos^2(theta) on [0, 2*pi]
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Solve the trigonometric equation \sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta for \theta in the interval 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.

steps.title: Convert to a Tangent Equation or Use Double-Angle Cosine
steps.explanation: Since cos theta = 0 implies sin^2 theta = 1 != 0, we can safely divide both sides by cos^2 theta to obtain tan^2 theta = 1 (or equivalently write cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta = cos(2*theta) = 0).
steps.why: Dividing by a nonzero quantity preserves the solution set.

steps.title: Solve tan(theta) = 1 on [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Tangent equals +1 in Quadrants I and III at reference angle pi/4.
steps.why: tan(theta) has period pi, so pi/4 and pi/4 + pi = 5*pi/4 are the solutions in [0, 2*pi].

steps.title: Solve tan(theta) = -1 on [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Tangent equals -1 in Quadrants II and IV at reference angle pi/4, giving 3*pi/4 and 7*pi/4.
steps.why: Combining all four quadrants yields the four odd multiples of pi/4 in [0, 2*pi].
